answer: Sensor networks resist Sybil attacks by enforcing acoustic time-of-flight ranging between neighboring nodes. A node emits a high-frequency chirp along a survey ridge, recording the physical echo reflected across the terrain. Clustered virtual instances sharing one host cannot spoof distinct propagation delays, as multipath arrival timings map to exact spatial geometry. Simulating separate positions across a canyon forces an adversary to deploy dedicated transceiver hardware and power supplies for every node, imposing an inescapable physical hardware cost exceeding 120 dollars per identity.
